direction_as_read: positive_weak: one 6-week RCT in functional dyspepsia met its primary outcome at 1920 mg/day; pooled lipid and liver results favor extract on surrogates; one pilot reports transaminases rising
summary: Labels print artichoke leaf or leaf and stem extract at 500 to 750 mg (600 mg on two), one whole herb extract, and 100 mg in a combination; four carry a digestive category. One study meets the reading bar: 244 patients with functional dyspepsia, 1920 mg/day for 6 weeks, primary symptom score favoring extract over placebo (14653829). A Cochrane review rates the artichoke result low certainty on 1 study of 244 participants (37323050). Lipid and fatty liver analyses favor extract on surrogates (28609140, 34569671, 41270328, 35763310); the trials read name no primary outcome in the abstract (29520889, 29193419) or no dose (41274796), and 41274796 reports AST rising. This is the strongest finding in the batch. No credit is recommended because the studied amount is about 2.5 to 4 times what a single serving prints; a clinician could read the digestive labels differently. Abstracts only.
question_for_clinician: One 244-person RCT in functional dyspepsia at 1920 mg/day met its primary outcome (14653829). Does it support credit for leaf extract labels printing 500 to 750 mg a serving, four with a digestive category, given the dose gap and that servings per day were not checked? Agent recommendation: no credit, and this one deserves a real look.

stop_or_hold: Whole herb extract (DSLD 269954) is not the leaf extract tested. LVR Formula (294008, 295528) prints 100 mg in a combination. Label directions for servings per day were not read. Six label rows (18368, 30958, 288774, 307554, 294008, 295528) carry canonical_id artichoke rather than globe_artichoke.
